uncited: Transparency and Blending Models define how 3D Gaussian primitives are composited into a 2D image, addressing the limitations of standard front-to-back alpha blending which requires strict depth sorting and assumes non-overlapping primitives.

These models range from hybrid approaches that balance performance and accuracy [3294-hybrid-transparency.md] to analytic volumetric integration that eliminates projection artifacts [4440-analytic-transmittance-3dgs.md], and order-independent methods that bypass sorting entirely [7562-sparseoit-rasterizer.md].

All methods in this family operate on 3D Gaussian primitives defined by mean $\boldsymbol{\mu}$, covariance $\boldsymbol{\Sigma}$ (or scales and orientation), opacity $o$, and color $\mathbf{c}$ (or spherical harmonic coefficients).
The core challenge is computing the pixel color $C$ and accumulated alpha $\alpha$ given a camera ray.
Standard splatting projects 3D Gaussians to 2D ellipses, computes a 2D alpha mask, and blends them in screen space.

These models modify the blending or shading stage: some refine the depth metric used for sorting, others integrate the 3D density function directly along the ray, and others use weighted averages to bypass sorting.
All assume the Gaussians are sorted or processed in a manner that approximates front-to-back accumulation to ensure correct occlusion.

For relighting, splats must carry physical material attributes: normal, roughness, reflectance (specular strength), and albedo (diffuse color) [4464-ref-gaussian-deferred-surfel-rendering-with-split-sum-ibl.md].
These are stored in a parallel Material Buffer aligned with the Splat Buffer [4464-ref-gaussian-deferred-surfel-rendering-with-split-sum-ibl.md].
For self-shadowing, a virtual "sun camera" is constructed to simulate a directional light source [4487-3d-gaussian-splatting-self-shadowing-t_light.md, 4489-light-space-rasterization-for-t_light.md].

This camera is placed at a large distance with a narrow field of view (FOV) to minimize parallax error to below 2% [4487-3d-gaussian-splatting-self-shadowing-t_light.md, 4489-light-space-rasterization-for-t_light.md].
Both relighting (for cache locality) and shadowing (for correct front-to-back accumulation) require sorting.
Relighting uses spatial locality algorithms like Morton codes [4464-ref-gaussian-deferred-surfel-rendering-with-split-sum-ibl.md].
Shadowing sorts Gaussians by depth relative to the sun camera [4487-3d-gaussian-splatting-self-shadowing-t_light.md, 4489-light-space-rasterization-for-t_light.md].

During the light pass for shadowing, the projection covariance is not expanded by $0.3I$ and no amplitude compensation is applied, preserving the main camera pass's sampling expansion [4487-3d-gaussian-splatting-self-shadowing-t_light.md].

In shadowing calculations, sun camera framing, sorting, coverage, and threshold branches are treated as constants to prevent incorrect gradient propagation [4487-3d-gaussian-splatting-self-shadowing-t_light.md, 4489-light-space-rasterization-for-t_light.md].

Originating from the need to improve view synthesis quality and rendering stability in 3D Gaussian Splatting, these methods address the linearization errors and sorting artifacts inherent in standard rasterization.
Analytic Transmittance derives from volumetric rendering theory, applying 1D Gaussian integration along rays [4440-analytic-transmittance-3dgs.md].
Hybrid Transparency and SparseOIT address the computational bottlenecks of sorting large numbers of fragments in real-time rendering [3294-hybrid-transparency.md, 7562-sparseoit-rasterizer.md].
